newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate panel backs Cohen as defense chief.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate panel backs Cohen as defense chief.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Armed Services Committee on Wednesday recommended Senate confirmation of former Sen. William Cohen to be secretary of defense, the first Republican in President Clinton's cabinet.
The Senate immediately began debate on the nomination for a quick confirmation vote.
Sen. John Warner, a senior Republican on the committee, predicted its vote on Cohen would be unanimous.
He said all committee members present voted to recommend Cohen's confirmation and said he was sure other members would also. He did not say how many still had to vote.
Defense Department spokesman Ken Bacon said Tuesday that Cohen would be sworn in to replace William Perry as secretary of defense quickly after his Senate confirmation.

Cohen said at his confirmation hearing before the committee earlier in the day that the United States intended to have its peacekeeping troops out of Bosnia in 18 months even if European allies kept a peace mission there longer.
